messages:
Maya: Heads-up — new customer pilot (FinEdge) wants a temporary model lock for their onboarding window. They asked for 45 days where we won’t auto-upgrade their catalog entry unless they opt in.
Tom: That’s a significant ask. We should distinguish between "no auto-upgrade" and "no emergency fixes". Can we allow security/safety hotfixes?
Maya: Customer accepts emergency fixes but wants a heads-up + a canary path. They specifically called out zero-DRIFT on embeddings for their search index.
Jules: Proposed plan: 45-day lock that auto-expires. Canary rollout: 2% -> 10% -> 30% over 48h with checkpoints. Health gates: quality delta <= 1.0% (measured on seeded prompts), p95 latency delta <= 120ms, error-rate delta <= 0.3%. Immediate pause + rollback on gate breach.
Priya: Bench spec (suggested): small bench suite combining 1k customer samples + 1k canonical probes. Metrics: semantic-similarity on embed pairs, top-k precision for rerank, and latency. Pass if quality loss <= 1% and p95 latency within 120ms of baseline.
Maya: Draft bench YAML for clarity:
```
bench_name: finedge-onboard-small
sample_count: 2000
categories: [customer, canonical]
metrics:
  - embed_cosine_drop_pct
  - rerank_precision_at_5
  - p95_latency_ms
pass_thresholds:
  embed_cosine_drop_pct: <= 1.0
  rerank_precision_at_5: >= baseline - 0.01
  p95_latency_ms: <= baseline + 120
reporting: per-route, per-tenant token breakdown
```
Tom: Execution ownership: Eng-ML runs bench and signs data validity. Product approves prompt set and customer acceptance criteria. Eng-Platform builds the canary automation with auto-rollback hooks. Eng-Infra evaluates a tiny reserved capacity for FinEdge business hours.
Jules: For the model pin semantics: treat this as a "maintenance-window lock" — we keep the model in the catalog entry but continue to apply emergency patches. Any non-backwards-compatible model change requires explicit customer opt-in.
infra-bot: INFO: Reserved-capacity check queued (#CAP-1291). ETA ~36h.
Maya: Commercials: recommend a small onboarding credit (15%) for the lock window and a signed SLO for latency during business hours. Also include a 10-day notice before any planned change post-lock.
Priya: If bench fails, allow two remediation attempts (customer + eng-ml) inside a 10-day remediation window. After that, product and legal to discuss next steps.
Legal Bot: REMINDER: Draft the temporary-lock clause: auto-expire, emergency-patch carve-outs, notice periods, data residency and audit logging requirements, and termination conditions. Also include standard export-control language.
Maya: Next steps: 1) Eng-ML to kick off bench today (target results in 72h). 2) Eng-Platform to prototype canary pipeline and rollbacks. 3) Eng-Infra to confirm reserved-capacity cost and hours. 4) Legal to provide clause draft for SOW. I'll prepare the customer comms.
Tom: +1. Please capture the exact seed prompts we use for embed drift measurement and keep samples immutable for the duration of the trial.
Maya: Will do — I'll store the seed set in the trial artifacts and link in the SOW. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
